newsitem.title: USA: U.S. magician Harry Blackstone Jr. dies at 62.
newsitem.headline: U.S. magician Harry Blackstone Jr. dies at 62.

text.p: Harry Blackstone Jr., a magician known for his lavish shows and spectacular illusions, died at the age of 62 apparently from pancreatic cancer, an official said on Thursday.
The San Bernadino County coroner's office said Blackstone died on Wednesday at Loma Linda University Medical Centre, 60 miles (95 kms) east of Los Angeles.
Blackstone carried on the tradition of magic on a grand scale first practiced by his father Harry Blackstone Sr., who also was known as "The Great Blackstone."
The younger Blackstone was introduced to magic at the age of 6 months, disappearing and mysteriously reappearing in his father's shows.
He went on to create one of the longest-running magic shows on Broadway and took his act abroad, appearing in Europe, Asia and Australia.
He also wrote a book, "The Blackstone Book of Magic and Illusion," and created special effects for the bands Earth, Wind and Fire and New Kids on the Block.
Blackstone was twice named magician of the year by the Academy of Magical Arts and was awarded the academy's Star of Magic, one of only 11 magicians, including his father, to be so honoured.
Born in Three Rivers, Michigan, Blackstone studied in Pennsylvania before moving to Los Angeles where he received his bachelors degree at the University of Southern California.
After serving in the military with the Army Security Agency, Blackstone followed in his father's footsteps. He was survived by his second wife, Gay, and several children from his first marriage.
